co_other_side_the_2.blurb: A bouldering sector within Hartman Rocks, the recreation area just outside Gunnison. It holds about fifteen problems, a modest tally next to the hundred-plus scattered across the wider area. Difficulty is centred on the middle of the scale, with the largest group around V3, a handful of easy warm-ups and a couple of V4s, plus one standout near V6. The stone at Hartman is granite, solid in places and crumbly in others, so test holds before pulling hard. The wider area is a multi-sport playground, so bouldering is only one part of a visit.

co_ra.blurb: Ra is a tall granite fin above the town of Empire, in an alpine setting along the highway to the north. The fifteen routes here are almost all bolted, with a single trad line, and the grades run from the low 5.10s up through the 5.13s, with most of the climbing in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. Several lines stretch to multiple pitches, which makes it a good choice for longer sport days. The main walls face west. Expect loose rock and a high-country feel, wear a helmet, and check yourself for ticks after the walk back.

co_new_economy_cliff.blurb: This short, steep bolted wall is on the canyon's south side in Clear Creek, roughly a mile above Tunnel 3 west of Golden. Around fifteen bolted lines, nearly all single pitch and fairly short, are split into a few sections beside a prominent white corner on the right. Grades start at 5.10 and are concentrated in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a single hard boulder problem on the side. Every route carries a financial name. Reaching the base means a creek crossing from the roadside pullout, which can be awkward when the water is up.
co_new_economy_cliff.approach: Leave the car at the roadside pullout and wade across the creek to the cliff, which stands directly opposite.

co_mitty_boulder.blurb: The largest single block in the Mitty Area of Castlewood Canyon State Park, a short way off the park trail. It packs in around fifteen problems, and the range is unusually wide for one boulder: easy openers at the bottom, a cluster of strong mid-grade lines around V5 to V7, and a few at V8 and V9 for the hardest-core visitors. Several of the lines are well liked by repeat climbers. It suits a session where beginners and strong boulderers can both find something, though the top end is serious.

co_isis_buttress.blurb: Isis Buttress is a traditional-only sector on the Book, part of Lumpy Ridge above Estes Park, tucked between two deep clefts on the left side of that formation. The granite here offers about fifteen routes, from the 5.8 range up to a few 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.10 and low 5.11 bracket. Crack systems, flakes and dihedrals dominate, and a number of the best lines are testpieces for the ridge. It tends to be quieter than the busier Lumpy walls. Loose rock around some belays makes a helmet sensible.
co_isis_buttress.approach: Follow the usual trail toward the Book, then bear left at the foot of the Pages Wall and pass the vertical cracks; the first cleft on the right leads up to the buttress.

co_cave_buttress.blurb: A smaller wall tucked into the Mother's Buttress complex in Unaweep Canyon, in the Grand Junction area. Fifteen granite routes, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines, are concentrated in the 5.11 range, with a couple of easier trad options below that and one or two harder at the top. Some lines run two pitches. The approach is the same as for Mother's Buttress; at the cliff, move a little up and to the right. Pairing the two in one day is easy.
